description.p: Splitlane is a native terminal workspace for running coding agents in parallel. Launch Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Pi, or any CLI agent in real panes, keep each session visible, and react when one needs input.

ul.li: One-click coding-agent launchers with per-session status tracking
Horizontal and vertical split panes with drag-to-resize, up to 32 panes
Branch-aware workspaces with rename, quick-switch, and session restore
In-app Git diff viewer and branch review prompts for agents
MCP bridge so capable agents can read other panes without copy/paste
JSON-RPC 2.0 IPC for local automation and integrations
Native Rust/GPUI rendering with Wayland and X11 support on Linux

description.p: A lead agent now hears when a session it opened has finished, "splitlane ps" and "status" report agent sessions, "splitlane read" returns the screen as well as the history, and panes keep their script names across a restart.
On macOS the app can update itself again: earlier versions refused every release and have to be replaced by hand once.

An agent in a pane can open agent sessions of its own and work through them: each is a row in the rail under the one that opened it, and a session that is waiting for you says so in a notification whichever way Splitlane learned of it. The skill that teaches Claude Code and Codex the commands is installed at every start.

Updates are checked for while the app stays open, a worktree is removed when its project closes if nothing in it would be lost, and background git no longer runs programs named by a repository's own configuration.
Codex and Claude Code no longer show as running before their first message, and every package ships the licenses of its dependencies.
Free access for agents can now be turned on only from Settings, not by editing the config file.
A freshly started agent without hooks no longer shows as running until its first message, and the window has a title on Linux.
